```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(20181024)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Innes_2018_stavudine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Innes_2018_stavudine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00761-18> (open access, PMC6201115)

Stavudine is a thymidine-analogue nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitor.
Its active moiety, stavudine triphosphate, is formed inside cells, and the
mitochondrial toxicity that limits stavudine's use is thought to track the
intracellular triphosphate rather than plasma stavudine. WHO lowered the adult
dose to 30 mg twice daily; Innes 2018 asked what paediatric dose gives the same
intracellular exposure.

The model links the oral stavudine dose directly to stavudine triphosphate in
peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC). Plasma stavudine was not measured,
so the first-order "appearance" rate `ka` lumps absorption, cell uptake and
phosphorylation, and all clearances and volumes are apparent and expressed in
cell units: 10^12 cells/h and 10^12 cells. Concentrations are fmol per 10^6
cells.

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Innes_2018_stavudine")
mod
```

# Population

Twenty-four HIV-positive adults and 24 prepubertal (Tanner stage 1-2)
HIV-positive children were enrolled in Cape Town, South Africa; one child was
excluded for non-adherence, leaving 23 children and 188 samples (Innes 2018
Results and Table 1). Adults: median age 36 years (range 26-51), weight 83 kg
(62-158), fat-free mass 47 kg (39-77), 1 of 24 male. Children: median age 8
years (4-11), weight 23 kg (18-31), fat-free mass 19 kg (14-25), 12 of 23
male. All were virally suppressed for more than 12 months on first-line
antiretroviral therapy.

Children received 0.5 mg/kg stavudine oral solution twice daily and adults
20 mg capsules twice daily for 7 days. On day 7, PBMC samples were taken
predose and at either 1, 2 and 6 h or 3, 4 and 8 h after the morning dose.
The LLOQ was 3 to 3.47 fmol/10^6 cells; the 2 samples below it were handled
with the M3 method.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Innes_2018_stavudine")()$population)
```

## Units

Table 2 gives clearances in 10^12 cells/h and volumes in 10^12 cells, with
concentrations in fmol/10^6 cells, but does not state the dose unit the model
was fitted with. The model takes the dose in mg of stavudine and converts it
1:1 by moles to stavudine triphosphate using the stavudine molecular weight
(224.21 g/mol): 1 mg per 10^12 cells is `1e6 / 224.21` = 4,460 fmol per 10^6
cells. That conversion is not printed in the paper, so it is checked here
against two printed numbers. At steady state, `AUCtau = F * Dose / CL`.

```{r unit-check}
fac <- 1e6 / 224.21
cl_ffm <- function(ffm) 454 * (ffm / 47.2)^0.75
unit_check <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Adult 30 mg AUCtau, FFM 46 kg (in silico adult median)",
    "Adult 30 mg mean steady-state concentration, FFM 46 kg"
  ),
  Paper = c(300, 25),
  `This model` = c(30 * fac / cl_ffm(46), 30 * fac / cl_ffm(46) / 12)
)
knitr::kable(unit_check, digits = 1,
             caption = "Typical-value check of the mg-to-fmol conversion (Results and Discussion).")
stopifnot(abs(unit_check$`This model` / unit_check$Paper - 1) < 0.05)
```

The adult in silico cohort median fat-free mass is 46 kg (Table S2). The
match to within 1% on AUC and the Discussion's "simulated median steady-state
concentration of 25 fmol/10^6 cells" confirms the molar conversion and the
units of CL.

## Variability percentages

Table 2 reports IIV and IOV as "approximate coefficient of variation". Monolix
estimates `omega`, the standard deviation of the log-normal random effect, and
`omega` itself approximates the CV; the exact log-normal CV would be
`sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`. The model therefore encodes `omega^2` as the square
of the printed percentage over 100 (e.g. IIV CL `0.304^2 = 0.0924`). The exact
reading `log(1 + 0.304^2) = 0.0883` would differ by under 5% on the variance.

# Typical-value checks

The children's column of Table 2 is the adult typical value rescaled to the
children's median FFM of 19.1 kg. Table S1 reports the medians of the
individual alpha and beta half-lives.

```{r typical}
typ <- function(ffm) {
  cl <- 454 * (ffm / 47.2)^0.75
  vc <- 2569 * (ffm / 47.2)
  q <- 469 * (ffm / 47.2)^0.75
  vp <- 7500 * (ffm / 47.2)
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  disc <- sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)
  c(CL = cl, Vc = vc, Q = q, Vp = vp,
    t_alpha = log(2) / ((s + disc) / 2), t_beta = log(2) / ((s - disc) / 2))
}
child_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("CL", "Vc", "Q", "Vp"),
  `Table 2 child` = c(230, 1037, 238, 3027),
  `This model, FFM 19.1 kg` = typ(19.1)[1:4]
)
knitr::kable(child_tab, digits = 0, caption = "Children's typical values (Table 2).")
stopifnot(abs(child_tab$`This model, FFM 19.1 kg` / child_tab$`Table 2 child` - 1) < 0.01)

hl_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Group = c("Adults (FFM 47.2 kg)", "Children (FFM 19.1 kg)"),
  `Alpha t1/2 (h), Table S1` = c(1.8, 1.3),
  `Alpha t1/2 (h), model` = c(typ(47.2)[["t_alpha"]], typ(19.1)[["t_alpha"]]),
  `Beta t1/2 (h), Table S1` = c(26, 19),
  `Beta t1/2 (h), model` = c(typ(47.2)[["t_beta"]], typ(19.1)[["t_beta"]])
)
knitr::kable(hl_tab, digits = 1, caption = "Disposition half-lives against Table S1 (medians of individual estimates).")
```

The typical half-lives (1.8 h and 24.7 h in adults, 1.4 h and 19.7 h in
children) agree with the Table S1 medians of the individual estimates.

# Virtual cohorts

The paper simulated 100,000 adults resampled from 2,680 covariate sets and
100,000 children resampled from 7,930, neither of which is published. The
cohorts here reproduce their Table S2 summaries instead, with 200 subjects per
arm:

* adults: fat-free mass log-normal with median 46 kg and IQR 40-53 kg
  (Table S2), restricted to the Table S2 range 18-62 kg;
* children: weight log-normal with median 21 kg and IQR 16-25 kg, restricted
  to 7-55 kg (Table S2 range 6-55 kg; the dosing table starts at 7 kg), with
  fat-free mass taken as `WT * 17 / 21`, the ratio of the Table S2 medians.

Out-of-range draws are redrawn, not clamped.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20181024)
set.seed(20181024)
n_arm <- 200

draw_lnorm_band <- function(n, med, q1, q3, lo, hi) {
  sdlog <- (log(q3) - log(q1)) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- stats::rlnorm(n, log(med), sdlog)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

adults <- tibble::tibble(
  FFM = draw_lnorm_band(n_arm, 46, 40, 53, 18, 62),
  WT = NA_real_,
  arm = "Adult 30 mg",
  dose = 30
)

child_wt <- draw_lnorm_band(n_arm, 21, 16, 25, 7, 55)

# Table 3 weight bands: WHO 1 mg/kg guideline and the proposed 0.5-0.75 mg/kg
# guideline (mg per dose, twice daily).
who_dose <- function(wt) {
  dplyr::case_when(wt < 10 ~ 9, wt < 14 ~ 15, wt < 25 ~ 20, TRUE ~ 30)
}
new_dose <- function(wt) {
  dplyr::case_when(wt < 10 ~ 7.5, wt < 14 ~ 10, wt < 25 ~ 15, wt < 60 ~ 20, TRUE ~ 30)
}

children <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(WT = child_wt, arm = "Children, WHO 1 mg/kg", dose = who_dose(child_wt)),
  tibble::tibble(WT = child_wt, arm = "Children, proposed", dose = new_dose(child_wt))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(FFM = WT * 17 / 21)

cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(adults, children) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    `FFM median (kg)` = median(FFM),
    `Dose median (mg)` = median(dose),
    `Dose median (mg/kg)` = median(dose / WT)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated cohorts (200 per arm).")
```

# Simulation

Doses are given twice daily for 10 days (20 doses; the 26 h beta half-life
needs about 9 half-lives to reach steady state) and the last 12-h interval is
sampled densely. Every record carries `OCC = 2`, so each subject's
between-occasion effects on bioavailability and ka are drawn once and held for
the whole course (see Assumptions).

```{r simulate}
tau <- 12
n_dose <- 20
t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
obs_times <- t_last + c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12)

doses <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, t_last, by = tau)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
obs <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::mutate(OCC = 2L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, FFM, OCC)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "FFM", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, arm, WT, dose), by = "id")
```

## Steady-state NCA with PKNCA

Time is re-based to the start of the last dosing interval.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last) |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, tad, Cc)
dose_df <- cohort |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, tad, dose)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ tad | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ tad | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = tau, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, WT, FFM), by = "id")
```

# Comparison against the paper's simulations

Results, "Dosing optimization": adults on 30 mg twice daily, median (IQR) Cmin
13 (10, 19), Cmax 45 (38, 53), AUC 300 (238, 380); children on the proposed
weight bands, Cmin 13 (9, 18), Cmax 49 (40, 58), AUC 300 (238, 379).

```{r nca-compare}
fmt_q <- function(x) {
  q <- stats::quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
  sprintf("%.0f (%.0f, %.0f)", q[2], q[1], q[3])
}
summ <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmin_med = median(cmin), cmax_med = median(cmax), auc_med = median(auclast),
    Cmin = fmt_q(cmin), Cmax = fmt_q(cmax), AUC = fmt_q(auclast)
  )

paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~Cmin_paper, ~Cmax_paper, ~AUC_paper,
  "Adult 30 mg", "13 (10, 19)", "45 (38, 53)", "300 (238, 380)",
  "Children, proposed", "13 (9, 18)", "49 (40, 58)", "300 (238, 379)",
  "Children, WHO 1 mg/kg", "not reported", "up to double the adult value (Fig. 2)", "not reported"
)
summ |>
  dplyr::left_join(paper, by = "arm") |>
  dplyr::select(arm, Cmin, Cmin_paper, Cmax, Cmax_paper, AUC, AUC_paper) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Arm = arm,
    "Cmin, simulated" = Cmin, "Cmin, paper" = Cmin_paper,
    "Cmax, simulated" = Cmax, "Cmax, paper" = Cmax_paper,
    "AUC0-12, simulated" = AUC, "AUC0-12, paper" = AUC_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state exposure, median (IQR); units fmol/10^6 cells and fmol/10^6 cells x h.")
```

The paper's tables give medians, so the medians are compared through
`ncaComparisonTable()`:

```{r nca-table}
ref_medians <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~PPTESTCD, ~value,
  "Adult 30 mg", "cmin", 13,
  "Adult 30 mg", "cmax", 45,
  "Adult 30 mg", "auclast", 300,
  "Children, proposed", "cmin", 13,
  "Children, proposed", "cmax", 49,
  "Children, proposed", "auclast", 300
)
sim_medians <- summ |>
  dplyr::filter(arm %in% ref_medians$arm) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, cmin = cmin_med, cmax = cmax_med, auclast = auc_med) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-arm, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "simulated")
cmp <- dplyr::left_join(ref_medians, sim_medians, by = c("arm", "PPTESTCD"))

nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = dplyr::select(cmp, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES = simulated),
  reference = dplyr::select(cmp, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES = value),
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmin = "fmol/10^6 cells", cmax = "fmol/10^6 cells", auclast = "fmol/10^6 cells*h")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated vs published medians (* marks > 20% difference).")

adult_cmp <- cmp[cmp$arm == "Adult 30 mg", ]
child_cmp <- cmp[cmp$arm == "Children, proposed", ]
stopifnot(
  # Adults: the reference arm, whose cohort is summarised by FFM alone.
  # A mis-transcribed CL, volume, dose or unit factor moves every median by
  # tens of percent.
  all(abs(adult_cmp$simulated / adult_cmp$value - 1) < 0.10),
  # Children: the paper's paediatric cohort is unpublished, so the medians
  # carry a cohort-construction difference (see below) on top of the
  # sampling noise.
  all(abs(child_cmp$simulated / child_cmp$value - 1) < 0.20)
)

who_vs_adult <- summ$cmax_med[summ$arm == "Children, WHO 1 mg/kg"] /
  summ$cmax_med[summ$arm == "Adult 30 mg"]
who_vs_adult
stopifnot(who_vs_adult > 1.2)
```

The adult reference arm reproduces the paper's medians to within 5%. WHO
1 mg/kg dosing gives a markedly higher median Cmax than the adult reference,
as Figure 2 shows. The simulated IQRs are wider than the paper's; see
Assumptions.

Children on the proposed weight bands come out about 15% higher than the
paper on AUC and Cmax (Cmin about 10% higher). The model itself is not the
cause: the adult typical values reproduce the paper exactly and the
children's Table 2 values to within 1%. The difference comes from the
paediatric simulation inputs, which the paper does not publish in full:

* Table 3 as printed gives 15 mg to children of 14-19.9 kg and 10 mg to
  children of 10-13.9 kg, which is 0.72-1.07 mg/kg, mostly above the 0.5-0.75 mg/kg
  range the table's own header and footnote state. The weight bands are
  applied here exactly as printed; if the paper's simulations used lower
  doses in these bands, its paediatric medians would be lower than ours.
* The paediatric cohort here approximates the paper's 7,930-child covariate
  set from its Table S2 summary (see Virtual cohorts).

The Discussion also quotes, for children on 0.5 mg/kg, a simulated Cmin of
10.9 and Cmax of 41.4 fmol/10^6 cells. The typical-value solve below, for a
child at the Table S2 median weight and FFM, is about 15% lower. That gap
goes the other way from the weight-band gap, which again points to the
unpublished paediatric cohort rather than to the model.

```{r discussion-check}
typ_child <- tibble::tibble(id = 1L, FFM = 17, OCC = 2L)
typ_child_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(time = seq(0, t_last, by = tau), amt = 0.5 * 21, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tibble::tibble(time = seq(t_last, t_last + tau, by = 0.05), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, FFM = 17, OCC = 2L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
typ_child_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_child_ev,
                                 returnType = "data.frame")
tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("Cmin", "Cmax"),
  `Paper Discussion (0.5 mg/kg)` = c(10.9, 41.4),
  `Typical child, 21 kg, FFM 17 kg` = c(min(typ_child_sim$Cc), max(typ_child_sim$Cc))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Children on 0.5 mg/kg twice daily, fmol/10^6 cells.")
```

## Figures 2 and 3

```{r fig23, fig.height = 8}
adult_med <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "Adult 30 mg") |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(auclast, cmin, cmax), median)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), names_to = "metric", values_to = "adult")

nca_wide |>
  dplyr::filter(arm != "Adult 30 mg") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(auclast, cmin, cmax), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::left_join(adult_med, by = "metric") |>
  dplyr::mutate(metric = factor(metric, c("auclast", "cmin", "cmax"),
                                c("AUC0-12", "Cmin", "Cmax"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(WT, value)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0.8 * adult, ymax = 1.2 * adult),
            fill = "grey85", inherit.aes = FALSE,
            data = function(d) dplyr::distinct(d, arm, metric, adult)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_grid(metric ~ arm, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "Stavudine triphosphate exposure (fmol/10^6 cells; x h for AUC)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figures 2 (WHO 1 mg/kg weight bands) and 3 (proposed 0.5-0.75 mg/kg
weight bands) of Innes 2018. The grey band is the simulated adult median
+/- 20% on 30 mg twice daily. WHO dosing sits above the band across most of
the weight range. The proposed bands bring exposure down towards it, with
the highest values in the 14-19.9 kg children, where the printed 15 mg dose
is largest per kilogram. The paper's Figure 3 shows its medians inside the
band; ours sit at its upper edge (see above).

## Typical profiles

```{r typical-profiles}
typ_ev <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:2, FFM = c(47.2, 19.1), dose = c(20, 0.5 * 23),
  label = c("Adult, 20 mg (FFM 47.2 kg)", "Child, 0.5 mg/kg at 23 kg (FFM 19.1 kg)")
)
typ_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typ_ev |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 6 * 24, by = 12)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  typ_ev |> tidyr::crossing(time = seq(6 * 24 - 1, 6 * 24 + 12, by = 0.1)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(OCC = 2L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
typ_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(typ_ev, id, label), by = "id")
ggplot(typ_sim, aes(time - 6 * 24, Cc, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after the day-7 morning dose (h)",
       y = "Stavudine triphosphate (fmol/10^6 cells)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Typical-value day-7 profiles under the study regimens, on the time scale of
Figure S1 (individual observed profiles).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose unit and molecular weight.** The paper does not state the dose unit
  used in fitting. The model takes mg of stavudine and converts 1:1 by moles
  with the stavudine molecular weight 224.21 g/mol; the check above reproduces
  the printed 30 mg adult median AUC (300) and steady-state concentration (25)
  to within 1%, which confirms the conversion.
* **Residual error form.** The paper says only "combined additive and
  proportional model". The Monolix default combined form,
  `y = f + (a + b * f) * e` (`combined1()`), is used. The additive term is
  small (0.6 fmol/10^6 cells against concentrations of 10-50), so the choice
  has little effect.
* **Variability scale.** Table 2's "approximate %CV" values are read as
  Monolix `omega` (the log-scale SD), so `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2`.
* **Occasions.** The model has two occasions as fitted: `OCC = 1` for the
  dose preceding the predose sample and `OCC = 2` for the sampled day-7 dose.
  The paper does not say how occasions were assigned in its 100,000-subject
  simulations. Here every dose carries `OCC = 2`, so the IOV on F and ka acts
  as a per-subject effect for the whole course. If the paper redrew F for each
  dose, the steady-state AUC would average over many doses (the 26-h beta
  half-life spans about four dosing intervals) and its IQR would be narrower,
  which would explain why the simulated IQRs here are wider than the printed
  ones while the medians agree.
* **Simulation cohorts.** The paper's in silico cohorts (2,680 adults and
  7,930 children from Stellenbosch University) are not published. Their
  Table S2 medians and IQRs are reproduced with log-normal draws; children's
  FFM is taken proportional to weight with the Table S2 median ratio 17/21
  rather than computed from height, age and sex with the Al-Sallami equation.
* **WHO weight bands.** Table 3 lists the WHO 1 mg/kg guideline only from
  7 kg; the 7-9.9 kg band (9 mg) is applied to the few simulated children
  below 10 kg, and the paper's restriction to children over 2 years is not
  modelled.
* **Age, sex and renal function** were tested and had no effect, so the
  model has no covariates other than FFM. The paper notes the model should
  not be used for children younger than 2 years, where maturation is
  expected.
* **Table S1** (adults 20 mg: Cmin 9.3, Cmax 32, AUC 232) holds medians of
  the 24 observed adults' individual estimates, not model predictions, so it
  is not used as a gate. The typical adult AUC at 20 mg is
  `r round(20 * fac / 454)` fmol/10^6 cells x h.
* No erratum to Innes 2018 was found (Europe PMC correction links and an
  erratum search, checked 2026-11-25).
